prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim. Injury: wrist fracture. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1279; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened following a rear-end collision at a signalized intersection. Insured vehicle struck the rear of claimant's vehicle. Police report obtained and reviewed. Liability appears probable against our insured based on the reported facts. Claimant reports wrist pain and was transported to the emergency department by ambulance.

Entry 2: Claimant is now represented by counsel. All further contact to go through the attorney's office. Letter of representation received and filed. Requested itemized medical records and wage documentation through counsel. Insured advised not to discuss the claim directly with the claimant or their attorney.

Entry 3: Medical records received from emergency department. Imaging confirms a fracture of the distal radius of the claimant's wrist. Orthopedic follow-up noted with recommendation for casting and possible surgical evaluation. Treatment is ongoing. Reserve reviewed and adjusted upward to reflect the injury severity and anticipated specials.

Entry 4: Spoke with claimant's attorney regarding the status of the file. Counsel indicated the claimant has missed time from work and is requesting documentation from the employer. Employer wage verification form sent to counsel for completion. Attorney stated a demand package will follow once treatment reaches a stable point. Discussed the need for an independent medical examination and noted it will be scheduled through counsel.

Entry 5: Reviewed file with supervisor. Liability position unchanged. Awaiting the demand package, updated treatment notes, and completed wage verification before evaluating settlement value. Diary set to follow up with counsel in thirty days. Litigation risk noted as moderate given the fracture and representation; will reassess on receipt of the demand.
